quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes. It is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be cited.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way. You do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to drive all the way across the tracks before entering them. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions coming up ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when someone passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help the other vehicle move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way rules?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to let others go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to let others go first.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Consider the situation at every intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it prevents a collision.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell you to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn after slowing and checking traffic.
You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
You may turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal your left turn three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror often as you slow down. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without hard braking. Carefully turn back onto the road. Check for nearby traffic before re-entering.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. Be prepared to stop your vehicle to prevent injury.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction may cross the center to pass.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with great caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive within the speed limit and slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: If you come to a flooded roadway, what should you do?

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through, as the water is unlikely to be too deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded water. You cannot tell how deep it is or how strong the current is. Your car could be swept away or become submerged.

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive under the influence of medication that affects your driving?

options.text: Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of anything that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train after the first one passes. Do not proceed until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge from the right side. Be ready to make room for merging vehicles.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign tells you the right lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If your vehicle starts to slide, remove your foot from the gas, do not brake, stay in your lane, and let the vehicle slow down.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap that is large enough to enter safely. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing that is being lowered or raised:

options.text: If a train is not too close.
If your vehicle will not damage the gate.
If you look carefully in both directions first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at railroad crossings mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What message appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers in the lane with the broken line may pass. Drivers in the lane with the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds make it harder to stop and increase crash damage. The faster you drive, the more powerful the impact if you crash.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: No one can park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot
Only when you are slowing down

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right
Hiking trails ahead and to the right
Hotel ahead and to the right
Hospital ahead and to the right

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that hospital emergency services are to the right.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway
When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels when parked uphill or downhill. This keeps your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so a rear-end hit won't push you into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake hard and hold it
Hold the wheel tight and use light braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tight and use light braking
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Release the gas pedal and brake lightly. Slow down gradually. Pull off the road in a safe place when possible.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: How do you safely enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead
Speed up and let other vehicles make way

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic behind and beside your vehicle before changing lanes. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care
Stop and proceed when a green light appears
Stop and proceed when the way is clear

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If both yellow lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; a curving road is ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal. When you are going very slow, apply the brakes gently and pull to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to stay away from the stopped vehicle.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to stay away from the stopped vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes if possible to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down well below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line, only drivers on the side of the dashed line can cross to pass. Drivers on the side of the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal after you start moving into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can be hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before you change lanes. Signal 100 feet in advance on residential streets. Signal five seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: What color are the lines that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of the road. They separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs show information about services for drivers, such as rest areas, food, gas stations, or hospitals nearby.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see if someone is tailgating or trying to pass. If a car is too close, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Check both left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because cars from the left are closer than those from the right. Also check across the entire intersection to make sure the path is clear.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas pedal and avoid braking right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: What factors affect how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and how much traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you first see rain, snow, or sleet. These conditions make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, you should drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey before the others?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, road work flag persons, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should they do?

options.text: Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting the car.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the car.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving because your mind is on something else. Take time to calm down and focus before you drive.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens, what must you do?

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right of way to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens. Move to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, what must you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down when you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: Is it illegal to drive next to a motorcycle in the same lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there seems to be enough room. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: You are behind a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay no more than one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their side mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the vehicle stops suddenly.
